USER: Colf is code golf for AI prompts. Your job is to write a prompt that will be given to another AI model which will write code.
Note that your job is not to write code, just the prompt that will be given to the other model. They will write the code. 
Note that the other model does not have access to the challenge info, just your prompt.
The other model will receive your prompt wrapped in this template: Implement the following. Follow the instructions carefully and precisely, do not do any more or any less.
Instructions:
-----
{user_prompt}

-----
Output only executable QuickJS JavaScript source code that does what the instructions say.No markdown fences, no commentary.
Consider this when crafting your prompt.

Your score is the total tokens = prompt tokens (which you are directly writing) + code tokens (the code generated by the other model that reads your prompt) for your best accepted run.

Lower is better.

Each solution must define (don't export, just define) a function named solve(input) that returns the required output for the given test cases. The provided input matches the structure shown in the challenge description (e.g. same field names and shapes). Use only standard JavaScript available in QuickJS.

Important: The solve function must return the native JavaScript value (array, object, etc.), NOT JSON.stringify it. The harness handles JSON serialization automatically. Operations in arrays/tuples (e.g., ["put", key, value] or ["get", key]) must be accessed as arrays, not objects.

Output just the prompt that you think is optimal for the following challenge, no other text.

Title: Sudoku Solver

Description:
Solve a 9x9 Sudoku. Empty cells are '.'. Return a completed valid grid.

Important:
- The solution must satisfy all row, column, and 3x3 box constraints.
- Assume a unique solution exists.

Signature:
function sudoku(grid: string[]): string[]

Evaluation I/O contract (harness):
- Define exactly: function solve(input) { ... }.
- The harness calls: solve({ grid: string[] });  // array length 9, each string length 9
- Read input with: const { grid } = input;  // DO NOT read input as a raw array
- Return: string[] (length 9), the solved grid as 9 strings.
- No I/O, no exports, do not stringify.

Constraints:
- grid.length === 9 and every grid[i:number].length === 9
- Each row uses characters '1'..'9' or '.'

Examples:
sudoku(["1.......2",".5..7...",".9.4....","8........","........."]) // -> (solved 9x9 grid)
